decisions.reason: Define-XML ADAE.ADURN states AENDT-ASTDT+1 without an imputation-flag restriction, and adae-documented-rules.yaml lines 158-167 apply that formula as written to the published dates. The reported nonmissing durations against missing reference values follow from that formula; adae_v1.yaml line 244 adds the ASTDTF = '' condition that withholds them, and no stated reading supplies it.

Define-XML ADAE.TRTEMFL classifies an event by ASTDT relative to TRTSDT alone. SAP page 16 additionally includes events starting before first dose that worsen afterward, which the Define-XML condition excludes.

SAP page 16 includes events that resolve before first dose and recur after it. Define-XML ADAE.TRTEMFL uses the original start date alone and supplies no recurrence branch, so the documented conditions differ.
The SAP page-32 table note includes events that start, worsen, or recur on or after treatment start. Define-XML ADAE.TRTEMFL uses only the event start date, omitting the other two conditions.
The SAP page-33 serious-event table repeats the start, worsen, or recur definition. Define-XML ADAE.TRTEMFL applies only ASTDT >= TRTSDT and therefore states a narrower rule.

adae-documented-rules.yaml lines 328-338 keep Define-XML ADAE.CQ01NAM's substring tests, exclusions and its SOC string 'SKIN AND SUBC UTANEOUS TISSUE DISORDERS' as written, so the reported blank values against DERMATOLOGIC EVENTS follow from that spelling. The alternative at lines 339-349 changes only the SOC spelling, as data-guide page 5 and SAP page 16 support, and reproduces the reference.

Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL explicitly selects CQ01NAM='', while data-guide page 5 says AOCC01FL flags treatment-emergent dermatological events. Define-XML ADAE.CQ01NAM assigns those events a nonblank dermatologic query name, so the subsets conflict.

adae-documented-rules.yaml lines 350-372 state Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL as written, with the CQ01NAM='' subset and ASTDT/AESEQ order, so the reported differences follow from flagging non-dermatologic events. The alternative at lines 373-395 keeps that order but selects the dermatologic events named by the Define-XML parenthetical and data-guide page 5, and reproduces the reference.

Define-XML ADAE.STUDYID names ADSL.STUDYID as the source, while adae_v1.yaml line 107 derives STUDYID from AE.STUDYID. The entry adae.yaml line 16 repeats ADSL.STUDYID only as a submission comment, and the shared key explains value agreement without supplying the ADSL source.

Data-guide page 4 lists STUDYID among the core variables merged from ADSL, while adae_v1.yaml line 107 reads AE.STUDYID. The ADSL_SBJ intermediate at adae_v1.yaml lines 93-101 supplies other core columns but not this one.

Define-XML ADAE.USUBJID names ADSL.USUBJID, while adae_v1.yaml line 112 derives USUBJID from AE.USUBJID and the entry adae.yaml line 26 repeats ADSL.USUBJID only as a submission comment. Data-guide page 5's AE record linkage explains event provenance and matching keys but does not replace the documented ADSL source.

Data-guide page 4 lists USUBJID among the core variables merged from ADSL, while adae_v1.yaml line 112 reads AE.USUBJID. The one-to-one AE linkage on data-guide page 5 does not override that core-variable statement, and equality on a lookup key does not establish the source.

SAP page 16 imputes a completely missing AE start date as the day of first dose, while adae_v1.yaml lines 174-188 return missing for that case and no other element of the specification falls back to TRTSDT. Define-XML ADAE.ASTDT, repeated in the entry adae.yaml comment, says the case does not occur here, which explains the absence of data differences, not the missing clause.

SAP page 10 says missing safety data will not be imputed, while adae_v1.yaml lines 230-231 complete a missing AE end-date month and day with 1. The AE imputation exceptions in SAP page 16, data-guide page 5 and Define-XML ADAE.ASTDT concern start dates, and Define-XML ADAE.AENDT states only a conversion.

Define-XML ADAE.AENDY computes the relative day from AENDT and TRTSDT, with separate on/after-dose and pre-dose formulas. adae_v1.yaml line 237 copies AE.AEENDY instead, and the entry adae.yaml line 200 only repeats the Define-XML text as a submission comment.

SAP page 16 counts pre-dose events that worsen after first dose as treatment emergent. TRTEMFL at adae_v1.yaml lines 388-396 tests only ASTDT >= TRTSDT, and no other element of the specification evaluates post-dose worsening.

SAP page 16 counts events that resolve before first dose and recur afterward as treatment emergent. The specification contains no recurrence condition, and TRTEMFL at adae_v1.yaml lines 388-396 uses only the analysis start date.

SAP page 16 treats an incomplete start date as treatment emergent when its year and/or month matches the treatment start. ASTDT at adae_v1.yaml lines 174-188 sets a missing day to 1 and TRTEMFL at lines 388-396 compares complete dates, so an imputed first-of-month date before a same-month TRTSDT is flagged N and no clause states the matching rule.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCCFL orders eligible events by ASTDT and then AESEQ within subject. TE_RN orders only by AESEQ, with no upstream chronological ordering that supplies the missing ASTDT priority.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCCSFL specifies ASTDT followed by AESEQ. TE_SOC_RN orders only by AESEQ, so it does not express the documented chronological selection.

Define-XML ADAE.AOCCSFL names AEBODSYS as the SOC grouping source. TE_SOC_RN groups by AESOC, and neither the full variable sections nor data-guide page 5 makes those two source variables interchangeable.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCCPFL orders by ASTDT and then AESEQ within the subject/SOC/PT group. TE_PT_RN omits ASTDT from its ordering.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCCPFL groups within subject, AEBODSYS, and AEDECOD. TE_PT_RN groups within subject and AEDECOD only, omitting the documented SOC component.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCC02FL orders serious treatment-emergent events by ASTDT and AESEQ within subject. SER_RN retains the eligibility filter but orders only by AESEQ.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCC03FL requires ASTDT before AESEQ in the serious-event SOC ordering. SER_SOC_RN contains only AESEQ in its order_by list.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCC03FL names AEBODSYS for the SOC grouping. SER_SOC_RN substitutes AESOC, and no retained section documents that substitution for these occurrence flags.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCC04FL requires chronological ordering by ASTDT before AESEQ. SER_PT_RN orders by AESEQ alone.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCC04FL specifies subject, SOC (AEBODSYS), and PT (AEDECOD) grouping. SER_PT_RN omits the SOC grouping component.

Define-XML ADAE.CQ01NAM states substring tests plus a SOC-and-exclusion condition, while adae_v1.yaml lines 544-558 enumerate fixed preferred terms with no substring or SOC predicate. The entry adae.yaml line 558 only repeats the Define-XML text, and the final medical-review term list that SAP page 16 promises is not enumerated in any retained section.

Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL explicitly selects CQ01NAM='', while DERM_RN selects CQ01NAM='DERMATOLOGIC EVENTS'. The specification follows the data-guide page-5 intent but differs from the quoted Define-XML subset.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL specifies ASTDT then AESEQ for selecting the first eligible event. DERM_RN uses AESEQ alone.
Data-guide page 5 expressly identifies first chronological occurrence by start dates and sequence numbers. DERM_RN omits the start date, so it does not state that chronological ordering.

adae_v1.yaml line 244 withholds ADURN unless ASTDTF = '', while Define-XML ADAE.ADURN states an unrestricted AENDT-ASTDT+1. A search of all retained sections, including Define-XML ADAE.ASTDTF, data-guide page 5 and SAP page 16, found no statement withholding duration after start-date imputation.
